title: Paper Glide – Free Paper Plane Game with Upgrades (One Button)
description: Play Paper Glide free in your browser: launch a paper plane, hold to climb, release to dive, ride the updrafts and upgrade your plane to fly further every time.
body: Fling a cheerful paper plane off a hilltop and see how far it can glide over the town and the park. Hold to lift the nose and climb, release to dive and pick up speed. Turquoise updrafts carry you higher, golden rings give a burst of speed, and balloons and birds slow you down.

Every flight earns coins. Spend them between flights on bigger wings, a steadier tail, a heavier nose, a stronger launcher and a coin magnet, and watch the next flight go visibly further. Flights last from half a minute to a minute and a half, there is no text, and it works on phones, tablets, Chromebooks and desktops. Your best distance, coins and upgrades are saved automatically.
New here? Read how to play and the tips to fly further.

title: How to Play Paper Glide – Launch, Glide, Upgrade
description: Paper Glide controls in one line: tap to launch, hold to climb, release to dive. Learn how the launch meter, updrafts, rings, coins and upgrades work.
body: Paper Glide uses a single input: the mouse button, your finger, or the Space bar (the Up arrow and W work too).

Launch. Each flight starts on a hilltop slingshot with a meter that swings from red to green. Tap when the needle is in the green, at the top of the arc, for the strongest launch. A perfect tap gives a small extra boost.

Glide. While you hold, the plane's nose rises: it climbs but slows down. When you release, the nose drops: it dives and speeds up. If the plane gets too slow it stalls, wobbles and tips its nose down by itself until it has enough speed again.

The sky. Turquoise columns with white swirls are updrafts: fly through them to be lifted up. Golden rings give a burst of speed. Balloons and blue birds cost you speed if you bump into them. Coins float in arcs.
Landing. The flight ends when the plane touches the ground. Your distance in metres is your score; a yellow flag marks your best. You earn the coins you picked up plus one coin for every 15 metres.

Upgrades. Tap the orange arrow button (on the menu or after landing) to improve wings, tail, weight, launcher and magnet. Each has ten levels and every level costs a little more. The bag button opens a separate shop for paper colours, patterns and trails, which only change how the plane looks.

title: Paper Glide Tips: How to Fly Further
description: Practical tips to beat your best distance in Paper Glide: the launch, the best gliding speed, using updrafts, avoiding stalls and which upgrades to buy first.
body: Do not hold all the time. Holding makes the plane climb, but every climb costs speed, and a slow plane stalls and drops. Short taps that keep the nose just below level glide the furthest.
Find the sweet speed. Too fast and the air brakes you hard; too slow and you sink. A gentle, shallow descent with steady speed covers the most ground.
Dive to reach updrafts. If a turquoise column is ahead and a little below, release to dive into it, then tap gently while inside to ride it up as high as it goes.
Save speed for obstacles. A bird or a balloon takes a chunk of your speed. Climb over a balloon early rather than at the last moment.
Aim the launch. The needle swings at a steady rhythm. Watch one full swing, then tap just before it reaches the green end.

Upgrade order. The launcher and the wings make the biggest difference early on: a stronger launch starts you higher and faster, and better wings lose less height per metre. The magnet pays for itself once you collect coin arcs regularly, and the tail makes stalls rarer and recovery quicker.
Use the ×2 button. After landing you can watch an optional video to double the coins from that flight, which gets you to the next upgrade sooner.

title: Paper Glide FAQ – Saving, Upgrades, Ads and Devices
description: Answers about Paper Glide: is it free, is progress saved, what each upgrade does, how ads work, and which devices it runs on.
body: Is Paper Glide free? Yes. It runs in the browser with nothing to download and no account.
Is my progress saved? Your best distance, coins, upgrade levels and shop items are saved on your device (and to your account on portals that support it). Clearing the browser data resets them.

What does each upgrade do? Wings: the plane loses less height and keeps flying at lower speed. Tail: steadier and more responsive, with fewer stalls. Weight: keeps speed better in dives and after bumps. Launcher: a higher ramp and a faster launch. Magnet: picks up coins from further away.
Can I buy coins with money? No. There are no purchases. Coins come only from flying, the daily gift and the optional ×2 video after a flight.
Are there ads? On game portals there may be a short ad between flights, never during one. Videos to relaunch after landing or to double your coins are always optional.
What is the daily gift? The first time you open the game each day you get free coins. Coming back on consecutive days raises the gift for up to seven days.
Which devices does it work on? Phones and tablets (portrait or landscape), Chromebooks and desktop browsers. It is a small download of about 1.6 MB.

title: Paper Glide for Schools and Kids – Safe, Short, No Sign-up
description: Paper Glide is a text-free paper plane game that works on school Chromebooks: no chat, no purchases, no account and no personal data, with a gentle physics lesson inside.
h1: Paper Glide for classrooms and kids
body: Paper Glide has no chat, no purchases, no account and no personal data. A flight lasts from about 30 seconds to a minute and a half, which makes it a good short reward between tasks.
There is no text in the game, only numbers and pictures, so it works the same for children who are still learning to read and for students of any language.

It is a playful introduction to flight: climbing trades speed for height and diving trades height for speed, a plane that flies too slowly stalls, and rising warm air lifts gliders just as it lifts birds. Comparing the distance before and after an upgrade is a natural way to talk about cause and effect, and adding up coins and upgrade prices practises simple arithmetic.
It runs in the browser on Chromebooks, tablets and phones, in portrait or landscape, and loads in a couple of seconds (1.6 MB).
